markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (83%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set, but the second model disagrees and only 3 of 5 neighbors match.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 83%, Invasive 16% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | {InSitu} (90%) | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 1.0 | Not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Disagrees |
| Similar cases | 3/5 InSitu [F5] | Moderate support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Scored below typical; failed spot check, not a reason · Unreliable
- **Benign stroma or fat** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Scarce here; scarcity is linked to invasive [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 6) · ↓ invasive · Score typical; concept model leans away from invasive [F4] · Validated
- **Nuclear pleomorphism** (region 11) · ↓ invasive · Score low (standardized −1.8) · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions drops invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect classifier. Normal lobules and mitoses are Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- The second model (MUSK) picks a different top class; the 83% rests on one classifier.
- This simulated frozen section is degraded (resample, severity 3), which may shift probabilities.

## Check on the slide
1. **5, 1, 2**: top heatmap contribution toward invasive; look for stromal invasion versus duct-confined growth.
2. **6**: strongest tumor-infiltrating stroma score; confirm whether true invasion is present.
3. **3**: lateral-margin segment flagged tumor at margin (108 µm); confirm on slide [F7].
